title: fix: ndk.abiFilters in buildTypes.debug not applied to APK packaging
description: The ndk { abiFilters 'arm64-v8a' } block placed inside buildTypes { debug {} } is ignored by the React Native Gradle Plugin. All 4 ABIs (arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86, x86_64) end up in the debug APK, resulting in 121 MB instead of the expected ~28 MB. The fix is to move abiFilters to defaultConfig { ndk {} } which AGP always honours.

title: Phase 12 — Wire notificationService.ts scheduleAlarm through overlayAlarmBridge with fallback
acceptance_criteria: notificationService.ts scheduleAlarm(title, eventDate, taskId?) is refactored so that when the alarm firing moment arrives, the overlay path is preferred. Since the current implementation schedules via expo-notifications (OS-level scheduler that fires when the app may be closed), the refactor keeps the expo-notifications schedule as-is but ALSO stores enough metadata (taskId + title) in the notification's data payload so that when the notification fires and the app is foregrounded via response handler, the overlay CAN be triggered. Practically: add a new exported function fireOverlayAlarmNow(taskId, title) that calls overlayAlarmBridge.fireOverlayAlarm and, on {fired:'unavailable'|'permission_denied'}, no-ops (the underlying expo-notification already fired as the fallback). scheduleAlarm keeps returning the notification id but its content now uses a shorter body since the overlay carries the primary UX. Add setupOverlayAlarmResponseHandler(handlers) that subscribes to overlayAlarmBridge.onAlarmAction and routes done/postpone/reroll to the same handler shape as setupNotificationResponseHandler; returns a cleanup fn. Existing tests (notificationService.test.ts) still pass unchanged. No behavioral change when running in jest (bridge absent → no-op).

title: Phase 12 — overlayAlarmBridge.ts: JS facade with graceful fallback + event emitter
acceptance_criteria: New file overlayAlarmBridge.ts at repo root. Public API (default export object): fireOverlayAlarm(taskId:string, taskTitle:string): Promise<{fired:'overlay'|'unavailable'|'permission_denied'}>; dismissOverlayAlarm(taskId:string): Promise<void>; onAlarmAction(listener:(e:{taskId:string, action:'done'|'postpone'|'reroll'}) => void): () => void (returns unsubscribe). Named export isOverlayAlarmAvailable(): boolean. Test hooks: __setOverlayAlarmAvailable(v:boolean|null), __resetOverlayAlarmCache(), __emitOverlayAlarmAction(payload) so tests can drive the event path without a real native module. Implementation: lazy require('react-native').NativeModules.OverlayAlarm — caches null result so subsequent calls don't re-require; if module absent, fireOverlayAlarm returns {fired:'unavailable'} + console.warn once; if module.fireOverlayAlarm rejects with code 'ERR_OVERLAY_NOT_GRANTED', returns {fired:'permission_denied'}. onAlarmAction: when native module present, wraps NativeEventEmitter(NativeModules.OverlayAlarm).addListener('overlayAlarmAction', ...); when absent, subscribes to an internal listener set that __emitOverlayAlarmAction can drive. Mirrors the structural pattern of nativeAppControl.ts (getRawNative caching + test overrides). Exports a TypeScript OverlayAlarmAction type for consumers.

title: Phase 12 — OverlayAlarmService.kt: foreground service + WindowManager overlay
acceptance_criteria: New file android/app/src/main/java/com/anonymous/randomtime/overlayalarm/OverlayAlarmService.kt. Extends android.app.Service. onStartCommand handles two intent actions: ACTION_FIRE_OVERLAY (extras: taskId String, taskTitle String) which posts a foreground notification in a dedicated 'overlay_alarm_service' channel and inflates a WindowManager overlay via TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY with flags FLAG_NOT_FOCUSABLE|FLAG_LAYOUT_IN_SCREEN|FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON, gravity BOTTOM|CENTER_HORIZONTAL; and ACTION_DISMISS_OVERLAY which removes the view silently. Overlay layout built programmatically in Kotlin (no XML) — LinearLayout(VERTICAL) with a TextView for the task title (bold, ~18sp) and a horizontal LinearLayout of three Buttons: 'Done', 'Postpone', 'Re-roll'. Any button tap: sends a LocalBroadcastManager (or context-registered) broadcast with action com.anonymous.randomtime.OVERLAY_ALARM_ACTION and extras {taskId, action:'done'|'postpone'|'reroll'}, then removes the view and calls stopSelf(). Returns START_NOT_STICKY (one-shot alarm). onDestroy removes the view if still attached and unregisters the notification. Runs on API 26+ (foreground services require channel); guards startForeground call with foregroundServiceType=specialUse on API 34+.
